title: Hinduism: Brahman, Atman and Karma
welcome_lead: Step into the rich world of Hinduism, the oldest of the major world religions.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on Hindu beliefs in Brahman, atman, karma and dharma.
final_note: You can now explain Brahman, atman, karma and reincarnation in Hinduism.

concepts.def: The one ultimate reality in Hinduism.
Inner self or soul in each person.
Rebirth of the atman in a new body.
Right way of living; moral duty.
Liberation from the cycle of rebirth.

walkthroughs.body_html: In Hinduism, Brahman is the one ultimate reality behind everything. Each person has an atman (soul) which is part of Brahman. The many Hindu gods are seen as different ways to picture and worship this one reality.
Karma means actions and their results. Good actions lead to good outcomes, bad actions to bad ones — in this life or future lives. Karma keeps the soul in samsara, the cycle of rebirth.
Dharma is your duty — to live morally and well, according to your role and stage of life. The ultimate goal is moksha: liberation from rebirth, when the atman unites with Brahman.
